name: SC-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Timmons with large fundraising edge ($1.6M raised, outside support)
Democrat McClain minimally funded ($33K raised, $1.2K on hand)
No public polling; markets price ~94% Republican
model.rationale: Timmons holds a heavily Republican seat with a dominant fundraising advantage and outside backing, while McClain has raised almost nothing. With no polling and markets pricing the race around 94% Republican, the fundamentals point to a comfortable but not fully locked-down incumbent win.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or primary fallout for Timmons, or unexpected outside spending against him, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 4th District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent William Timmons is seeking another term after securing his party's nomination. He has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $487,000 in outside support, while Democrat Courtney McClain has raised only about $33,000 with minimal cash on hand. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but is not a factor.

No public polling covers this race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put Republican chances around 94 percent. The seat remains very likely to stay Republican, though the margin is not certain enough to call it entirely safe.
